title: Time to Cross a Bridge
summary: Given k workers and n boxes, each worker has specific times to cross the bridge to the right and back to the left, as well as to pick and put boxes.
statement: Given k workers and n boxes, each worker has specific times to cross the bridge to the right and back to the left, as well as to pick and put boxes. Workers are prioritized based on their efficiency, defined by the sum of their right and left crossing times, with a secondary condition based on their index if the sums are equal. The bridge can only be used by one worker at a time, and when unused, the least efficient worker on the right side is prioritized to cross, followed by the least efficient worker on the left side. Once enough workers have been dispatched from the left side to pick up all the remaining boxes, no more workers will be sent from the left side. The elapsed minutes at which the last box reaches the left side of the bridge are to be determined.
constraints: Each worker row gives left-to-right, pick, right-to-left, and put times.
When the bridge is free, a waiting right-side worker goes first; otherwise dispatch a left worker only while boxes remain.
Within one side choose the least efficient worker: greatest crossing-time sum, breaking ties by greatest original index.
Return when the final box finishes crossing back to the left; its put time is not included.
hints: Separate waiting workers on each bank from workers still picking or putting a box.
Use availability-time min-heaps for busy workers and priority heaps for waiting workers.
At each bridge-free time, release completed work, prefer the right queue, and otherwise dispatch left only if an unassigned box remains.
Event jumps skip idle time, and the queue priorities exactly implement the stated policy; the final right-to-left crossing determines the answer.
editorial: Event jumps skip idle time, and the queue priorities exactly implement the stated policy; the final right-to-left crossing determines the answer.

tests.explanation: Worker two is least efficient and returns the only box at time six.
Following right-side priority and worker efficiency delivers the third box at time fifty.
